figures.alt: Physical fixture, CAD assembly and MuJoCo representation
figures.caption: Figure 1. The declared B2 fixture in physical, CAD and simulator views. Appearance establishes recognizable geometry; each view supports different claims about structure and behavior.*

figures.alt: Physical grouping and executable body tree
figures.caption: Figure 2. Read the tree from top to bottom: the fixed housing supports one hinge, the link rotates at that hinge, and the two attached payload groups introduce no extra joints. The left sketch groups the same external mechanism physically.*

Figure 3. B0, B1 and B2 place equal 44 g assemblies at symmetric radii. G1 places them on one side. Each complete assembly includes its pin. These are declared positions in the 110 g teaching family.*

figures.alt: Matched conditions, physical and digital outputs, and three evidence levels
figures.caption: Figure 4. Declared conceptual comparison. Physical and simulated inputs must have compatible meaning and conditions; measured and predicted outputs must be aligned before comparison. The diagram contains no experimental trajectories.*
Figure 5. The physical-to-executable chain preserves selected information at each stage. Export transfers a representation; inspection establishes what was transferred.*

figures.alt: Trace a pin attachment point through the actual B2 model and its units
figures.caption: Figure 6. The same B2 attachment point at zero and +30° joint positions. The plot shows displacement from the joint in the world x–z plane; the table reports absolute world coordinates. The 7 mm axial offset is outside this projection. These are declared model coordinates, verified against MuJoCo, rather than hardware measurements.*

figures.alt: Visual geometry, a candidate collision simplification and inertial properties
figures.caption: Figure 7. Three descriptions of the same conceptual link: the visual surface retains holes, a candidate collision rectangle simplifies those surfaces, and the inertial panel marks the centre of mass while retaining the link outline. The supplied fixtures currently disable contact.*

Figure 8. The solid circle is the nominal bore. The dashed circle illustrates a possible smaller, offset as-built bore. Compare diameter and alignment rather than appearance alone; the difference is exaggerated and is not a measured tolerance.*
Figure 9a. Use the shaft centreline and mounting interfaces to orient the RS06 motor reference. Drawing values are manufacturer nominal values, not measurements of the available unit.*

figures.alt: RS06 fixture configurations shown as CAD renders
figures.caption: Figure 9b. Identify the fixed motor housing and moving link: M0 has no external fixture, B0 has the balanced link, B1 adds both large end payloads, and G1 has one large end payload. These are CAD renders, not physical photographs.*
